section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the Torah was given specifically on earth because mitzvos involve physical objects and because fulfilling them below refines the animal soul.
section.t: And the explanation is,
that regarding the reason why the Torah was given specifically down on earth,
there are two matters.
Because the drawing down through the mitzvos is when the fulfillment of the mitzvos is in physicality,
and also because through the fulfillment of the mitzvos below, the refinement of the animal soul is accomplished.
And this is what Moshe said: “Do you perform labor?… Is there an evil inclination among you?”
For the reason the Torah was not given in heaven to the angels is that then these two matters would be lacking.
“Do you perform labor that you need rest?”
Therefore it is not applicable for them to fulfill the mitzvah of Shabbos in physicality, and likewise regarding “Do not take [Hashem’s name in vain],”
honoring father and mother.
“Is there an evil inclination among you?”
Therefore, refinement of the animal soul is not applicable to them.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses two aspects of the connection between refining the animal soul and the giving of the Torah, and questions how the work of refining the animal soul can lead to the revelation of “Anochi.”
section.t: B)
And it can be said,
that regarding the connection of the refinement of the animal soul
(“Is there an evil inclination among you?”)
to the giving of the Torah,
there are two matters.
That through the fulfillment of the mitzvos given at the giving of the Torah, the refinement of the animal soul is accomplished,
as above.
And the refinement of the animal soul is also a preparation for the giving of the Torah.
Therefore we count the Omer before the holiday of Shavuos,
for the counting of the Omer is the refinement of the attributes of the animal soul,
and through this we merit the giving of the Torah on Shavuos.
And based on this,
the matter of “Is there an evil inclination among you?”
(the latter matter in Moshe’s response)
is similar to the matter of “To Egypt you descended”
(the first matter in Moshe’s response),
that regarding the connection of the Exodus from Egypt to the giving of the Torah,
there are two matters.
That through the giving of the Torah,
the drawing down and revelation of “Anochi Hashem Elokecha,”
there is accomplished “Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,”
and that the Exodus from Egypt is an introduction and preparation for the giving of the Torah,
as the simple interpretation of “Anochi Hashem Elokecha Who brought you out of the land of Egypt,”
that “Who brought you out of the land of Egypt” is a reason for “Anochi Hashem Elokecha.”
And it must be understood,
that the matter of the giving of the Torah is
(as stated in the opening of the giving of the Torah)
“Anochi Hashem Elokecha,”
that “Anochi” is His essence and Selfhood becomes “Hashem Elokecha,”
and how is it possible that through the work of refining the animal soul there will be a drawing down of Anochi?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the completeness of the Omer counting depends on serving God with “all your might,” which is the preparation for the revelation of Anochi, yet the primary work of the Omer is still the refinement of the animal soul.
section.t: C)
And behold, it is stated in the Midrash
on the verse,
“And you shall count for yourselves from the morrow of the Shabbos… seven complete weeks shall they be. When are they complete? When Israel does the will of the Omnipresent.”
And according to what is explained in many places,
that the matter of “doing the will of the Omnipresent” is specifically through the love of “with all your might,”
above measure and limitation,
it is understood,
that what the Midrash says, “When are they complete? When Israel does the will of the Omnipresent,”
is,
when the work of the Counting of the Omer is connected with the love of “with all your might.”
[And it is noteworthy,
that elsewhere our sages said
that “seven complete weeks” means that the seven weeks of the Omer begin on a Sunday and end on the Shabbos that is Shabbos,
for then they are seven complete weeks.
And it can be said that the connection of the two interpretations is,
that in those years when the seven weeks of the Omer begin on a Sunday and end on Shabbos,
it is easier,
that the work of the Omer be in the manner of “with all your might.”]
And superficially, it can be said,
that the connection of “doing the will of the Omnipresent”
(“with all your might”)
to the Counting of the Omer,
is,
because the Counting of the Omer is a preparation for the giving of the Torah,
and since the preparation for the giving of the Torah must be in two matters,
the Exodus from Egypt and the refinement of the animal soul,
therefore,
there must be in the Counting of the Omer
(in addition to the matter of refining the attributes of the animal soul,
also)
the work of “with all your might,”
above measure and limitation,
the departure from Egypt, from the term “narrow place” and limitation.
And it must be understood that according to this,
the work of “with all your might” is an indispensable preparation for the giving of the Torah,
and from that they said “When are they complete…” it implies that the primary matter of the Counting of the Omer,
the preparation for the giving of the Torah,
is the refinement of the attributes of the animal soul,
and the work of “with all your might” pertains only to the completeness of the preparation for the giving of the Torah.
And even more so it is not understood,
that since the matter of the giving of the Torah is the revelation of Anochi,
His essence and Selfhood which is infinitely above the order of Hishtalshelus,
the work appropriate for drawing down this revelation is seemingly the work of “with all your might”
(above the Hishtalshelus within man),
and nevertheless,
the primary work of the Counting of the Omer is the refinement of the attributes of the animal soul
[for in order to refine the attributes of the animal soul, it is specifically through the Godly soul clothing itself in the animal soul],
and through this the revelation of Anochi is drawn down.
